author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dutch payments company Adyen plans to expand further in India after sharply increasing its local workforce and securing licenses needed to process domestic and cross-border transactions.

The company had about 120 employees in India during the first half of 2026, ten times its 2023 headcount, Reuters reported. Adyen received payment-aggregator and cross-border licenses in 2024 and says it plans more hiring, though it did not give a target.

Adyen is modifying its platform for India-specific requirements, including data localization, recurring-payment mandates and the Unified Payments Interface. Its Indian business reported pretax income of 3.18 million euros in 2025, up from 1.45 million euros a year earlier.

The expansion places Adyen in a large but tightly regulated digital-payments market. The company is also preparing for so-called agentic commerce, in which software agents help initiate purchases, but adoption and regulation are still evolving. The figures describe completed reporting periods and announced plans; they are not a live measure of revenue, transaction volume or valuation.
dek: The Dutch payments company has increased its India workforce tenfold since 2023 and is adapting its platform to local payment rules.
headline: Adyen plans further India expansion as local business grows
